about: The physical constants and units the physics is computed with, each with its source (registry/README.md).

a4.note: the standard tuning frequency, A above middle C: MIDI 69

t60-db.note: a reverberation time's fall: the time a sound takes to decay by 60 dB

milli.note: SI's milli: thousandths in one (ms in a second)

steel-density.note: the handbooks' steels span the range; 7850 the value engineers take (490 lb/ft^3). A wound string's stiffness enters the models only as E d^4, so its d is taken as the steel cylinder of its density and E what gives its measured stiffness

arundo-donax-density.material: Arundo donax L. (giant cane): the single reeds of clarinets and saxophones and the double reeds of oboes, English horns and bassoons
arundo-donax-density.note: clarinet reeds' cane: 450 (Facchinetti, Boutillon & Constantinescu 2003; Pinard, Laine & Vach 2003), 520 (Guimezanes 2008; Taillard et al. 2014), 500 (Chatziioannou 2010; the review gives Ukshini & Dirckx 2020 too, who do not state it)

arundo-donax-longitudinal-modulus.material: Arundo donax L. (giant cane): the single reeds of clarinets and saxophones and the double reeds of oboes, English horns and bassoons
arundo-donax-longitudinal-modulus.note: dry, along the fibres, 1 mm specimens: 5.0 (±0.7) GPa; 1.5 mm: 3.0 (±0.2). The range the others' (Gaillard, Koehl & Gazengel 2024, Table A2): 3 to 9.5 along a reed from heel to tip (Guimezanes 2008, Table A3), 10 (Facchinetti 2003; Chatziioannou 2010), 14 (Taillard et al. 2014). Its tissues by indentation: the fibres' sheaths about 7 GPa, the parenchyma 2 to 3, the vascular bundles 1.5 to 2 (Kawasaki et al. 2017, doi:10.1002/jemt.22889)

arundo-donax-longitudinal-modulus-wet.material: Arundo donax L. (giant cane): the single reeds of clarinets and saxophones and the double reeds of oboes, English horns and bassoons
arundo-donax-longitudinal-modulus-wet.note: soaked 15 minutes, as a reed is played: 1 mm specimens 3.1 (±0.4) GPa, 1.5 mm 2.1 (±0.3)

arundo-donax-transverse-modulus.material: Arundo donax L. (giant cane): the single reeds of clarinets and saxophones and the double reeds of oboes, English horns and bassoons
arundo-donax-transverse-modulus.note: dry, across the fibres: 1 mm 0.5 (±0.03) GPa, 1.5 mm 0.4 (±0.06); 0.2 to 0.5 along a reed (Guimezanes 2008), 0.4 (Facchinetti 2003; Chatziioannou 2010) (Gaillard, Koehl & Gazengel 2024, Table A2). Ten times softer than along them

arundo-donax-transverse-modulus-wet.material: Arundo donax L. (giant cane): the single reeds of clarinets and saxophones and the double reeds of oboes, English horns and bassoons
arundo-donax-transverse-modulus-wet.note: soaked: 1 mm 0.1 (±0.05) GPa, 1.5 mm 0.2 (±0.02); 24 times softer than along the fibres

arundo-donax-shear-modulus.material: Arundo donax L. (giant cane): the single reeds of clarinets and saxophones and the double reeds of oboes, English horns and bassoons
arundo-donax-shear-modulus.note: G_xz, along the fibres and through the thickness: 1.3 GPa (Facchinetti 2003; Chatziioannou 2010), 0.6 to 0.87 along a reed (Guimezanes 2008), 1.1 (Taillard et al. 2014)

arundo-donax-poisson.material: Arundo donax L. (giant cane): the single reeds of clarinets and saxophones and the double reeds of oboes, English horns and bassoons

arundo-donax-hysteresis-wet.material: Arundo donax L. (giant cane): the single reeds of clarinets and saxophones and the double reeds of oboes, English horns and bassoons
arundo-donax-hysteresis-wet.note: the share of the work of a slow bend lost as it is let go, soaked, along the fibres, 1 mm specimens (11.9, 16.1, 19.1 %); 1.5 mm 14.2 to 32.8 %, across the fibres 28.1 to 41.2 %: a quasi-static loss, not the reed's damping at its resonance

legere-longitudinal-modulus.material: Légère (polypropylene fibres in polypropylene): the synthetic single reed
legere-longitudinal-modulus.note: 1 mm specimens 7.5 (±0.3) GPa, 1.5 mm 5.9 (±0.2): half again cane's, and unchanged by water

legere-transverse-modulus.material: Légère (polypropylene fibres in polypropylene): the synthetic single reed
legere-transverse-modulus.note: 1 mm 1.9 (±0.1) GPa, 1.5 mm 1.8 (±0.01): four times softer than along its fibres, where cane is ten

legere-density.material: Légère (polypropylene fibres in polypropylene): the synthetic single reed
legere-density.note: isotropic polypropylene's, about 0.91 g/mL, as Légère's patent gives it (cited, not measured)

fiberreed-longitudinal-modulus.material: Carbon Fiberreed (carbon fibres in a matrix): a synthetic single reed

fiberreed-transverse-modulus.material: Carbon Fiberreed (carbon fibres in a matrix): a synthetic single reed

dalbergia-melanoxylon-gravity.material: Dalbergia melanoxylon Guill. & Perr. (African blackwood, grenadilla, mpingo): the bodies of clarinets, oboes, English horns and piccolos
dalbergia-melanoxylon-gravity.note: basic specific gravity: oven-dry mass over green volume, over water's density; its five records, tropical Africa (the database's references 58, 147, 192, 192, 200): 1.08, 1.13, 0.90, 1.20, 1.076; the median taken. Its hygromechanical constants measured by Alkadri et al. 2020 (doi:10.1007/s00226-020-01215-z), not yet fetched

acer-pseudoplatanus-gravity.material: Acer pseudoplatanus L. (sycamore maple, mountain maple): bassoons' and contrabassoons' bodies; the violin family's backs, ribs and necks
acer-pseudoplatanus-gravity.note: basic specific gravity: oven-dry mass over green volume, over water's density; Europe (references 28, 60)

acer-platanoides-gravity.material: Acer platanoides L. (Norway maple): the violin family's backs and ribs, bassoons' bodies
acer-platanoides-gravity.note: basic specific gravity: oven-dry mass over green volume, over water's density; Europe (references 158, 28)

picea-abies-gravity.material: Picea abies (L.) H. Karst. (Norway spruce, European spruce): the violin family's tops
picea-abies-gravity.note: basic specific gravity: oven-dry mass over green volume, over water's density; Europe (reference 28)

paubrasilia-echinata-gravity.material: Paubrasilia echinata (Lam.) Gagnon, H.C.Lima & G.P.Lewis (pernambuco, Caesalpinia echinata in the database): the violin family's bows
paubrasilia-echinata-gravity.note: basic specific gravity: oven-dry mass over green volume, over water's density; tropical South America (references 35, 44)

diospyros-crassiflora-gravity.material: Diospyros crassiflora Hiern (African ebony): the violin family's fingerboards, pegs and tailpieces
diospyros-crassiflora-gravity.note: basic specific gravity: oven-dry mass over green volume, over water's density; tropical Africa (references 136, 1, 137, 99, 40): 0.80, 0.99, 0.826, 0.90, 0.775, the median taken

acer-saccharum-modulus.material: Acer saccharum Marshall (sugar maple, hard maple)
acer-saccharum-modulus.note: its modulus in static bending at 12 % moisture, specific gravity 0.63 at 12 % (green: 10.7 GPa at 0.56); along the grain about 10 % above it (Table 5-1, note). Its elastic ratios at 12 %: E_T/E_L 0.065, E_R/E_L 0.132, G_LR/E_L 0.111, G_LT/E_L 0.063 (Table 5-1); its Poisson's ratios mu_LR 0.424, mu_LT 0.476, mu_RT 0.774, mu_TR 0.349 (Table 5-2)

picea-sitchensis-modulus.material: Picea sitchensis (Bong.) Carr. (Sitka spruce): soundboards and the tops of instruments made in America
picea-sitchensis-modulus.note: its modulus in static bending at 12 % moisture, specific gravity 0.40 at 12 % (green: 8.5 GPa at 0.37); red spruce (Picea rubens) 11.4 GPa at 0.40. Its elastic ratios at 12 %: E_T/E_L 0.043, E_R/E_L 0.078, G_LR/E_L 0.064, G_LT/E_L 0.061, G_RT/E_L 0.003 (Table 5-1)

wood-modulus-green-softwood-coefficient.note: a in E = a G^b, green softwoods (16,100 MPa)

wood-modulus-green-softwood-exponent.note: b in E = a G^b, green softwoods

wood-modulus-green-hardwood-coefficient.note: a in E = a G^b, green hardwoods (13,900 MPa)

wood-modulus-green-hardwood-exponent.note: b in E = a G^b, green hardwoods

wood-modulus-dry-softwood-coefficient.note: a in E = a G^b, softwoods at 12 % moisture (20,300 MPa); G their gravity at 12 %. Sitka spruce at 0.40 gives 9.5 GPa, measured 10.8

wood-modulus-dry-softwood-exponent.note: b in E = a G^b, softwoods at 12 % moisture

wood-modulus-dry-hardwood-coefficient.note: a in E = a G^b, hardwoods at 12 % moisture (16,500 MPa); G their gravity at 12 %. Sugar maple at 0.63 gives 11.9 GPa, measured 12.6

wood-modulus-dry-hardwood-exponent.note: b in E = a G^b, hardwoods at 12 % moisture

cartridge-brass-density.material: C26000 cartridge brass, 70 % copper and 30 % zinc (yellow brass): the saxophones' and most brass instruments' bodies and bells

cartridge-brass-modulus.material: C26000 cartridge brass, 70 % copper and 30 % zinc (yellow brass)

gold-brass-density.material: C23000 red brass, 85 % copper and 15 % zinc (instrument makers' gold brass): bells and leadpipes

gold-brass-modulus.material: C23000 red brass, 85 % copper and 15 % zinc (gold brass)
